summary: A completed booking prototype awaiting a barbershop's decision.
roleSummary: Prototype lead, backend architecture & teammate onboarding
contribution: Started ClipStack, built most of the prototype, and later onboarded a teammate who joined the project. My work focused on the backend architecture, booking workflows, and synchronization model across the customer, manager, and staff experiences.

decisions.title: Make booking conflicts explicit
decisions.reason: The design uses optimistic concurrency and conflict responses so competing edits can be resolved rather than silently overwriting a booking.

decisions.title: Plan for repeated requests
decisions.reason: Idempotent requests are part of the sync design: retrying after an interrupted connection should not create duplicate operations.

decisions.title: Move from Azure Functions to ASP.NET Core
decisions.reason: The prototype began with Azure Functions, but a conventional ASP.NET Core backend made the growing system easier to understand, extend, and scale as more features were considered.

lesson: The prototype is complete and further work depends on the barbershop's approval. The hardest part was choosing an architecture that could stay understandable while supporting the many features a full product would need; that led to replacing Azure Functions with ASP.NET Core.

architecture.description: Customer and manager Vue clients and a Kotlin Multiplatform staff app access an ASP.NET Core REST API backed by PostgreSQL. Mobile synchronization handles retries and booking conflicts explicitly.
architecture.source:
flowchart LR
        web[Customer and manager web] --> api[ASP.NET Core REST API]
        mobile[Kotlin staff app] <-->|offline sync| api
        api --> rules[Conflict and retry handling]
        rules --> db[(PostgreSQL)]

name: ClipStack
purpose: Booking prototype for an independent barbershop moving from paper calendars to low-friction customer booking and dependable staff workflows. The completed prototype covers customer and manager web experiences plus an offline-capable staff app, with explicit booking conflicts and retry-aware synchronization.
result: Completed prototype ready for stakeholder review

media.alt: ClipStack mobile prototype dashboard showing synchronized appointments and staff navigation
media.title: Mobile staff dashboard

coreStory: I started ClipStack to help an independent barbershop move from paper calendars to online booking and practical staff workflows. I built most of the prototype and later onboarded a teammate.

My focus was the backend architecture, booking workflows and synchronization across customer, manager and staff experiences. The prototype is complete; further development depends on the barbershop’s approval. Moving from Azure Functions to ASP.NET Core helped me keep the growing system understandable.
